title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Maritime Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Maritime Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)"

Fa Fa [2003] No. 4

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and all Maritime Courts:

In order to thoroughly implement the "Maritime Procedure Special Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the "Maritime Procedure Law") and further standardize maritime judicial activities, the 1258th Meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court discussed and adopted the "Maritime Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)" (hereinafter referred to as the "Forms"). These are now issued to you, and it is expected that they will be followed in maritime judicial work. The relevant matters concerning study and implementation are hereby notified as follows:

I. It is essential to deeply understand the significance of studying and implementing the "Forms," and to truly apply the "Forms" in maritime judicial practice to achieve uniformity in maritime litigation document forms. The formulation and issuance of the "Forms" is an important measure to fully implement the "Maritime Procedure Law," a significant symbol for maritime judicial work to respond to WTO accession and to uphold the principle of legal uniformity under the WTO rules, and also an important manifestation of the court's work theme of "justice and efficiency." Doing this work well is of great significance for unifying maritime judicial activities, improving the quality and efficiency of case handling, establishing a high image of the people's courts, and enhancing the authority of China's legal system.

II. It is necessary to seriously organize maritime judicial personnel to deeply study and implement the "Forms," and to achieve the standardization of maritime litigation documents as soon as possible. The "Forms" are highly specialized and rich in content; they serve both as standards for maritime judicial personnel in drafting adjudicative documents and as document samples for guiding parties in maritime litigation. Each Maritime Court and its appellate court shall set aside time to study the "Forms," promptly study and resolve issues encountered during study, so that every judicial personnel can deeply understand and skillfully apply them, ensuring the smooth implementation of the "Forms." Adjudicative documents produced after the implementation of the "Forms" shall conform to the requirements of the "Forms," and this shall be one of the conditions for the selection of excellent maritime and maritime-related adjudicative documents.

III. These "Forms" apply only to the contents covered by the "Maritime Procedure Law." The production of other maritime litigation documents shall still follow the "Court Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)" issued by the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on June 20, 1992. In maritime judicial work, the two sets of litigation document forms shall be used in conjunction. Where new litigation document forms have been formulated for a particular type of document, the original form for the same type of document shall no longer apply.

IV. For any document forms not covered by these "Forms" or the "Court Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)," each court may design its own forms based on the needs of maritime judicial work and use them uniformly within the court.

If any problems arise during the trial implementation of these "Forms," please promptly report them to our court.

March 18, 2003

Maritime Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)

Instructions

I. These litigation document forms are applicable only to the contents covered by the "Maritime Procedure Special Law." The production of other maritime litigation documents shall still follow the "Court Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)" issued by the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on June 20, 1992. In judicial work, the two sets of litigation document forms shall be used in conjunction. Where new litigation document forms have been formulated for a particular type of document, the original form for the same type of document shall no longer apply.

II. The heading of litigation documents for non-foreign-related maritime cases shall not be preceded by the words "People's Republic of China."

III. The appellate courts of Maritime Courts, when hearing maritime and maritime-related cases, shall refer to these litigation document forms when producing litigation documents.

IV. The phrase "This copy has been verified as identical to the original" shall be stamped by the clerk using a routine seal after verifying the accuracy of the document against the original; it need not be printed when producing the document.

V. For document forms shared by Maritime Courts and their appellate courts, the wording "People's Republic of China ×××× (Maritime) Court" shall be adopted, to be selected and used respectively.

VI. For any document forms not covered by these litigation document forms or the "Court Litigation Document Forms (Trial Implementation)," each court may design its own forms based on the needs of judicial work and use them uniformly within the court.
